page.overview:
What is Dune (novel)?

Dune is a science fiction novel written by Frank Herbert and published in 1965. A winner of the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Award Hugo Award] and [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebula_Award Nebula Award] for outstanding science fiction, Dune is popularly considered one of the greatest science fiction novels of all time, and is frequently cited as the best-selling science fiction novel in history. Dune spawned five sequels written by Herbert, and inspired a film adaptation by David Lynch, two miniseries made by the United States-based Sci-Fi Channel, computer games, the trilogy by Denis Villeneuve (Part One released in 2021, Part Two in 2024 and Part Three anounced for december 2026). A cinema adaptation should been made by Alejandro Jodorowsky, but it couldn't be done and that finally lead to the documentary movie directed by Frank Pavich Jodorowsky's Dune. There's as well series of prequels, interquels, and sequels co-written by Brian Herbert, the author's son, and Kevin J. Anderson.

Dune is set far in the future, amidst a sprawling feudal intergalactic empire, where planetary fiefdoms are controlled by Noble Houses that owe allegiance to the Imperial House Corrino. The first novel, modestly entitled Dune, tells the story of young Paul Atreides. Heir apparent to Duke Leto Atreides I from the planet Caladan, he and his family have to relocate to the planet Arrakis, an extremely arid world that is the universe's only source of the spice melange. In a story that explores the complex interactions of politics, religion, ecology, technology, and human nature, the fate of Paul, his family, his new planet and its native inhabitants, as well as the Padishah Emperor, the powerful Spacing Guild, and the secretive female order of the Bene Gesserit, are all drawn together into confrontations that will change the course of humanity.

The novel was originally serialised in the magazine, Analog, from 1963 to 1965 as two shorter works: Dune World and The Prophet of Dune.

Opening twenty-thousand years into the future, the human race has scattered throughout the galaxy, populating multiple planets ruled by aristocratic Houses who themselves answer to the galaxy's Imperial family House Corrino. Key is the control of the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the valuable spice melange. Spice gives those who ingest it an extended life and prescient awareness. Melange is crucial as it enables space travel. This domain is monopolized by the Spacing Guild; its Navigators use the spice to safely plot a course for the Guild ships via prescience using "foldspace" technology. So they can travel instantaneously to anywhere in the galaxy.

Also known as: Dune book, Dune 1965.
